verticalInfoCards.title: Rituals and Aarti
verticalInfoCards.note: A key ritual is bathing in the 22 holy water bodies (theerthams) within the temple complex, starting with a dip in the Agnitheertham sea.

quote.text: “Walking through the thousand-pillared corridor is like walking through time, each pillar whispering tales of devotion and royalty.”
quote.author: — A History Enthusiast

verticalInfoCards.description: The temple houses two lingams: one made of sand by Sita (Ramalingam) and another brought from Kailash by Hanuman (Viswalingam).

overview.title: Overview
overview.text: Ramanathaswamy Temple, located on Rameswaram island, is a major Hindu pilgrimage site, revered as both a Jyotirlinga and one of the four Char Dham destinations. It is renowned for its grand architecture, especially its spectacular pillared corridors, and its deep connection to the epic Ramayana.

mythology.title: Mythological Origin
mythology.text: After defeating the demon king Ravana in Lanka, Lord Rama wanted to atone for the sin of killing a Brahmin. On the advice of sages, he decided to worship Lord Shiva. He sent Hanuman to bring a lingam from Mount Kailash. As Hanuman was delayed, Sita created a lingam from sand, which was then consecrated by Rama. This is the main deity, the Ramalingam.

architecture.title: Architectural Highlights
points: The temple boasts the longest corridor among all Hindu temples in the world, with over 1200 intricately carved pillars.
It is a classic example of Dravidian architecture, with towering gopurams and massive walls.
The temple complex is spread over 15 acres.
There are 22 sacred water bodies or 'theerthams' inside the temple, and bathing in them is a significant ritual.
The construction and expansion of the temple were carried out by various rulers over several centuries.

significance.title: Spiritual Significance
points: It represents the southernmost of the 12 Jyotirlingas.
It is one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites.
A pilgrimage to Kashi (Varanasi) is considered incomplete without a visit to Rameswaram.
The ritual of bathing in the 22 theerthams is believed to wash away one's sins.

events.event: The original lingam was consecrated by Lord Rama.
The Pandya dynasty began the construction of the current stone temple.
Significant contributions and expansion by the Sethupathis of Ramnad.

items.text: Worship is first offered to the Viswalingam (brought by Hanuman) before the main Ramalingam.
A holy dip in the Agnitheertham (the sea in front of the temple) is the first step of the pilgrimage.
The nearby Dhanushkodi is believed to be the starting point of the Ram Setu bridge.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Rameswaram is a monumental testament to faith, history, and architectural grandeur. It is a sacred bridge between the traditions of Shaivism and Vaishnavism, offering a deeply purifying and spiritually fulfilling experience to every pilgrim.

aboutPostCards.title: Major Festivals
items: Maha Shivratri – Celebrated for 10 days with various rituals and processions.
Arudhra Darisanam – A significant festival in December-January.
Navaratri – Celebrated with grandeur, especially for the Goddess Parvathavardhini.

aboutPostCards.title: Nearby Attractions
items: Dhanushkodi – A ghost town at the south-eastern tip of the island with scenic beaches.
Pamban Bridge – India's first sea bridge, offering stunning train and road journeys.
Agnitheertham – The sacred sea shore for holy baths.
APJ Abdul Kalam Memorial – A memorial dedicated to the former President of India.

methods.title: By Road
methods.description: Rameswaram is well-connected by road to major cities in Tamil Nadu like Madurai, Chennai, and Kanyakumari.

methods.title: Nearest Railway
methods.description: Rameswaram Railway Station (RMM) is located on the island.

methods.title: Nearest Airport
methods.description: Madurai Airport (IXM) is the nearest, approximately 175 km away.

mapSection.title: Temple Location
mapSection.description: Located on Pamban Island in the Ramanathapuram district of Tamil Nadu, separated from mainland India by the Pamban channel.
